title.narrative: WGG- Feminist Leadership and Mentorship in India

description.narrative: The objective of the strategy is to destabilise these structures by ensuring new women leaders are represented in policy and decision making spaces as well in convenings and conversations.

The program strategy aims to capacitate new women leaders, including WWDs and young women, on feminist leadership to build inclusive movements and alliances. The program recognises power structures, both visible and hidden, that exist within movements.

sector.narrative: Support for feminist, women-led and women's rights organisations and movements, and institutions (governmental and non-govermental) at all levels to enhance their effectiveness, influence and substainability (activities and core-funding). These organisations exist to bring about transformative change for gender equality and/or the rights of women and girls in developing countries. Their activities include agenda-setting, advocacy, policy dialogue, capacity development, awareness raising and prevention, service provision, conflict-prevention and peacebuilding, research, organising, and alliance and network building

comment.narrative: As the indicator measures any new values occurring since the start of the intervention,the baseline value is set at 0
Through local-level political processes such as panchayat meetings

Around 170 YWLs and WWDs with whom Yuva is working to build their capacities, have demonstrated their leadership by participating in the political processes at various levels. They particited in Mahila sabha to raise issues related to toilet for PWDs, water, garbage disposal. They also raised their voices to stop voilence against YW in their neighborhood, negitiated with ealth service providers to improve assess to SRHR and worked to spread awareness against evil practices such as witchcrafts.15 YWLs emerged as leaders to take up GBVH relates issues at Gram Panchayat level and creating awareness among community women on the issues related to sexuality, marriage and decision making. They have done advocacy with govt and non-govt stakeholders, for this they have developed a booklet for storey telling. They are also running sanitary pad bank in their respective panghayats.Registration for voter ID card for self was done by 60 YLs and they also encouraged other adolescent girls about their voting rights. Some of them also supported women to fight against domestic violence. Supported enrollment of PWDs and also supported them in preparing handicapped certificate. As as result 12 PWDs received handiccaped certificate. One of the CREA India strategic partners, later reported the political participation of leadership demonstrated by 15 young girls. Thus, the target of 260 for the reporting period is achieved. Earlier, an achievement of 245 was reported, but now this information has been updated in the results.
Cumulative target spread across 2 yearsThrough local level political processes such as panchayat meetings

Women leaders of Sangram Panchayat (including young women and healthcare providers) took an initiative at the village council level to ensure that no woman undergoes surgery during childbirth and that all deliveries take place normally.These women leaders advocated on this issue with the Panchayat head, as a result of which the head gave priority to the matter. Now, pregnant women have been connected to Shri Satya Sai Hospital, where their regular health check-ups are being ensured.Women leaders, young women, and women Panchayat representatives are going into their respective communities and spreading awareness about the One Stop Center. They are informing other women that the One Stop Center provides assistance in cases of violence, harassment, or any kind of emergency, including legal counseling, general counseling, temporary shelter, and medical services. This initiative has led to a significant increase in awareness among women and adolescent girls in rural areas about their rights and the support services available to them.Women leaders participated in cross-learning visits to institutions such as the Childline, District Hospital, and One Stop Center. These exposure visits significantly enhanced their understanding of government support systems. As a result, these women have now begun to take independent leadership roles in raising their voices against violence and injustice faced by themselves and other women in their communities.Trained adolescent girls, who earlier participated in football training sessions, have now taken leadership roles in sports by representing their districts, divisions, and even the state in football tournaments. These girls have become strong symbols of confidence, teamwork, and gender equality within their communities.
